FRESH IN-THE-WILD REPRODUCTION (orchestrator session, 2026-08-20) — a SECOND independent occurrence,
on a different release hash from the one in the linked frangible-irongray-adouri RCA. This is no
longer a historical report; it broke live work minutes ago.

WHAT HAPPENED. A `rebar transition <ticket> in_progress closed` was running (the completion verifier
takes minutes, which is what makes the window wide). Mid-run the release directory backing the
process was removed, and the close died with:

  ImportError: cannot import name 'commit_impact' from 'rebar._engine_support'
  (/Users/joeoakhart/.local/state/rebar-dev/releases/d6841983c6754605f7c34c9f0bb8aab733e5dbd4.84448/
   src/rebar/_engine_support/__init__.py)

STATE CAPTURED IMMEDIATELY AFTER, which pins the mechanism precisely:
  * `~/.local/state/rebar-dev/releases/` contained exactly ONE directory:
    `b91f8f6830cc2e9eeee4db390dd8466e4c4256ae.86589`
  * `~/.local/state/rebar-dev/current` -> `releases/b91f8f6830...86589`
  * The path in the traceback, `d6841983c6...84448`, was NOT present — it had been pruned while the
    process that resolved it was still running.

So the failing process was executing out of a release that no longer existed, and the error names a
module that demonstrably exists in the source tree. That is the signature to key on.

CONSEQUENCE: the close FAILED and the ticket remained `in_progress`. Note the operational hazard —
the command exited such that a naive caller could read success while the state change did not
happen. Any automation that closes tickets in the background can silently no-op this way.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR YOUR REPRODUCTION PLAN: your ticket proposes synchronising two real processes
(pause an invocation before a late import, force-reinstall from a sibling, then release). This
occurrence confirms the shape WITHOUT needing `uv tool install --force` — an ordinary scheduled
prune produced it. So the reproduction does not depend on the uv trigger specifically; ANY removal
of the backing release during the window works. That may make your harness simpler: you can drive it
with a directory removal rather than orchestrating a real reinstall, then separately confirm that uv
force-reinstall performs an equivalent removal.

The window is wide because the late import sits AFTER a minutes-long LLM gate — so this is not a
narrow race requiring precise timing. It will keep recurring on any host whose updater prunes on a
schedule while long rebar operations run.
